1.explanation: lighthouse-core/audits/user-timings.js is where traceEvents are read, grouped into marks and measures, and returned by the audit. This is the place to add logic that ignores any timing events whose names start with “ad_” or “goog_”. Without filtering here, all injected ads timings flow downstream. The renderer, lighthouse-core/formatters/user-timings.js, consumes the audit’s output to build the report UI. Although most of the heavy lifting happens in the audit, the formatter should be reviewed (and potentially adjusted) to ensure it doesn’t re-include or render any events that slipped through, keeping the final report clean of irrelevant marks.
1.bug_scenario: When running the Lighthouse “user-timings” audit against pages that load Google Ads, every single blink.user_timing mark and measure—including those injected by Google (names prefixed with “ad_” or “goog_”)—ends up in the report. The screenshot shows dozens of “ad_slots_defined”, “ad_requested_from_server”, “goog_123_3_1_start/end”, etc., cluttering the “User Timing marks and measures” section. We need to filter out those irrelevant events.

2.explanation: The audit logic in audits/user-timings.js currently grabs every blink.user_timing event from the trace, without excluding ad_* or goog_* marks. That’s why all of the Google Ads–injected user timing marks appear in the report. The formatter in formatters/user-timings.js then renders every item the audit emits. To filter out irrelevant marks you’ll need to update the filtering logic in user-timings.js (e.g. drop names matching /^ad_/ or /^goog_/) and ensure the formatter still correctly displays only the remaining valid marks and measures.
